name: Pagiel
overview: Pagiel was a male leader from the tribe of Asher, serving as the head of his tribe during the census taken in the wilderness. He played a significant leadership role during the Exodus, representing Asher among the tribes of Israel. His position highlights his importance in the organizational structure of Israel at that time.
namesAndTitles: The name Pagiel appears only once in Scripture without a given meaning or special title. It is presented simply as a proper name in the book of Numbers, chapter 1, verse 13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Pagiel was the son of Ochran. Beyond this explicit father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pagiel's role as head of the tribe of Asher during the census underscores his responsibility in representing and leading his people during a pivotal moment in Israel's journey. This leadership position during the Exodus reflects the orderly and God-ordained structure established among the tribes. His mention in Numbers highlights the importance of tribal organization under God's guidance as Israel prepared for their inheritance.
